doing.t: Art pass 9: Haar Wyrm steam base retake (far-horn fix)
doing.why: Base redrawn (v3, both horns forward, steam-and-bone); review picture rebuilt and deployed for Sean. Step: full local suite before opening the PR.

queue: Art loop: PixelLab art for the seven placeholder guardians, Haar Wyrm first. Budget: 193 generations plus Sean's 50 USD of credits, all approved for this. Sean on facing (2026-11-06): strict east/west profile for anything that moves (walk, run, attacks, jumps); the south-east/south-west three-quarter stance, turned toward the camera, is welcome for animations where the figure stands still (idle, rest, talk, a guardian's intro or taunt). Update docs/art/enemy-style-guide.md (Facing, and 6 step 1a) to say so in the same PR, keep west as east mirrored, and give every character that has a still three-quarter clip a turn clip of 2 or 3 frames, generated in PixelLab from the three-quarter base (about one generation each), played forward from still to moving and backward from moving to still. Don't hand-fix drift in turn frames: Sean cleans those up himself. Copy each turn clip's frames to art/cleanup/<character>/turn/ for him, list the new ones on the workbench under "done" as ready for his cleanup, and have the importer prefer art/cleanup over the raw PixelLab output. Never overwrite or regenerate anything already in art/cleanup. Sean approves every base before animation (2026-11-06): for each new or redesigned character, make only its base first (the east profile and the south-east three-quarter stance, a few generations). Save one review picture to shots/<character>-base-for-approval.png: both views at 1x and 4x, next to the current in-game sprite and the hero for scale. Run python workbench/deploy.py (PYTHONUTF8=1) so it shows on the hosted Shots tab, and put "Waiting for Sean's OK on the <character> base" under "stuck". Generate no animations, turns included, for a character until a note from Sean approves its base. A note asking for changes means a retake of the base and a new review picture. While waiting, make bases for the next characters in the order (no more than three waiting at once) and otherwise do non-art work. Prompts for props (Sean, 2026-11-06: PixelLab once drew a light bulb on a figure's head when a stalk with an orb on its end was asked for): say what holds each prop and where it sits, one prop per sentence (Sean's wording that worked on the eel: "an anglerfish-style stalk with a dangling glowing orb"); scope a comparison to the part with "<creature>-style <part>", never "like a <creature>" or "like an anglerfish", which turns the whole body into that creature (the eel became a long skinny fish); keep a part's words physical (dangling, curving, fleshy) so it isn't read as an object, say what must stay clear when a prop could stray ("nothing on his head"), and give a glow a color rather than words like light, lamp or bulb. Check every base and frame for stray or moved props before anything goes to Sean. If a prop still wanders after one retake, generate the figure without it and add the prop with PixelLab's inpaint or the free pixelart_workbench, not more rerolls. Write these rules into the enemy style guide's prompt section in the same PR.

VFX pass: try PixelLab's VFX tool (pixellab.ai/create-vfx; the MCP tool vfx_workbench, free for subscribers, no generations spent) on one code-drawn effect first, a sword hit or a guardian death burst. Export the spritesheet PNG + JSON, play it in Godot next to the current effect, and keep it only if it reads better against the enemy style guide and passes the art loop review

Independent grade (pass 497, 5.3/10, up from 4.1): top defect is the player sprite's fidelity gap. The hero reads as a small soft low-detail hooded blob with no readable silhouette or gear detail, far below the environment art (and below the guardians the art loop is remaking). Upgrade the player sprite's silhouette, detail and animation read so it is the most polished thing on screen, per design bible 13.5 (the hero is made in PixelLab). Judge at 1x and 2x against the enemy style guide.

Independent grade (pass 497): flat lighting with no ambient occlusion. Walls meet floors and platforms meet backgrounds with hard unshaded seams, and lanterns rarely cast real light pools. Add contact shadows / AO where platforms and walls meet, and give light sources gradient pools, so surfaces read as lit volumes, not stickered tiles. Try it in code first (a cheap darken-at-seams pass) before any art generations.

Independent grade (pass 497): depth collapse and tile repetition. Trunks, mid platforms and the play layer share value and saturation, so the player gets lost against busy backdrops; brick and wall fields tile obviously. Strengthen atmospheric perspective (desaturate/darken the parallax back layers) so the play layer pops, and add tile variants so the grid's repeat unit stops reading.
done: Art pass 9: the Haar Wyrm steam base, far horn fixed. Sean's note e20c6ea1 (the 3/4 far horn curled backward) is answered: the head is redrawn as the steam-and-bone wyrm (pro create_character, 112px, 15 generations) with both horns rising from the crown and curving forward over the brow toward the muzzle — a matched pair in the east profile and the three-quarter, so the two views agree and the far horn no longer curls the wrong way. Paler/more bleached than the fog base (steam, not fog). First retake came out multi-headed ('three-headed serpent' read literally) and was discarded; the lesson ('name only the part the sprite is, not the whole creature') is now in the style guide step 1c. New committed tool tools/art/base_review.py builds the review picture. Base gates on Sean's OK (no animation, no haar_wyrm.gd change yet); fresh review deployed to the Shots tab. Budget 106.0 -> 76.0 generations + 50 USD (30 spent, credits untouched). Full local suite + CI green; squash-merged. No in-game change, so no captures and no fresh grade (held at pass-497 5.3/10).

Pass 499: the Haar Wyrm breathes steam, not fog (#557). Sean's top-queue note is shipped. MistBreath is now SteamBreath: a slow (95 px/s, was 150) gout that vents from the jaws, narrow at the mouth and billowing wider as it rolls, hotter and whiter than the fog with a heat shimmer, thinning and cooling as it goes; its hurt rect stays capped at 44 px (under a single jump's 72 px apex) so a jump or the tank walls still clear it, 12 damage, no parry, phase 3 on the flood. The tell leaks wisps and plays a rising steam hiss; a doused head goes out with a hiss and a last puff; the dry tanks steam; the epithet is 'Three Heads of Steam'. New steam-pipe haar_breath + a steam_hiss tell in sfxgen (local rng so only those two wavs change). Story carried through the bible (8.4, the Stillstone lines, the fog-lifts event row, 13.3 sound count 169), Ilka and the three Haar Spring signs: the wyrm is steam and bone, boiled the tanks dry, and the Haar's fog is its steam cooled over the marsh. Four new tests (speed/billow/lifetime, dodged by jump and walls, the tell floor, the doused puff); the guardian sheet and Stillstone test follow the rename; mutation-checked. Caught and fixed a CRLF-contamination gotcha (Python writes had corrupted trailing tokens, failing 44 bible-parse checks) — files normalized to LF. Full suite 8364 checks 0 failed; CI test+mix green (mix needed one rerun past an apt/ffmpeg flake); squash-merged; main fast-forwarded. Haar Wyrm arena recaptured (the steam-white head reads against the green solid head); no static shot shows the transient breath gout, and no before/after was posted — the old fog look is superseded by the gated base redraw anyway. Not a fifth/art pass, so no fresh independent grade.

Art pass 8: the guardians begin, the Haar Wyrm head base (#556). Wrote Sean's 2026-11-06 rules into the guide and bible first: the AAA art goal (bible 12.0), facing split into moving (strict profile) vs still (three-quarter), turn clips plus the art/cleanup importer preference, prop prompt-craft, and base-before-animation. Made the Wyrm solid-head base (create_character pro, 8-dir, 112px, 15 generations, balance 168->153, no credits) and a review picture on the Shots tab. NOTE: Sean's 'breathes steam, not fog' note synced in ~16 min after this run had already started/chosen pass 8, so the base is the old FOG look and is now superseded; the steam pass (queue top) will redo it as a steam wyrm. Local suite 8355 checks 0 failed; CI (test + mix) green; squash-merged; main fast-forwarded. No fresh independent grade: nothing visible shipped in-game (base gates on approval), and the pass-497 grade (5.3/10) is current in grades.json.

Pass 498: Carillon rains from a PixelLab sheet now. Sean's rain trial (2026-11-06) is done: the free VFX tool's slant_rain preset, stripped to its three drop depths and exported as a 32-frame sheet (assets/vfx/carillon_rain.png), tiled screen-wide in two parallax layers (far 2x/slow/faint, near 1x/fast/bright) so the 1 s loop never shows. New SheetRain node; it leans on the storm wind and thins to a drizzle once the Sky Spring breaks the storm (SheetRain.density, same spring:sky flag as Motes.SETTLES). Shot the same two Carillon rooms both ways (shots/rain-trial): the sheet reads as a driven storm with real depth where the code streaks barely showed, so the sheet is kept (SHIPPED; the streak field stays as the fallback). 1.57 ms a frame in the soak; new test + two rewritten; mutation-checked; bible updated; README playtest link pointed at the Yldenfall repo. For Sean: the sheet won, so other outdoor zones could take a light rain too — the Haar marshes most of all (a thin slow drizzle for the fog), the High Boughs an even fainter mist-rain. Left for you to decide. Captures of the spires rooms refreshed on the workbench.

Pass 497: Lithic Fracture, Sean's approved supporting spell (#554). A cascade of six stone columns erupts along the floor, 32 px and 0.08 s apart, stepping down ledges and stopping at walls and pits; 24 MP, 6 damage per column. Each foe struck once is slowed to half speed for 3 s (a new Enemy slow that can only lengthen a telegraph) and, unless a boss, staggered. Cracked stone seals (legend [) only this spell shatters hide four optional gold caches across three zones (hearthroot/heartwood/tower); the scroll (legend :) lies on the Kettleforge lift gallery. Code-drawn columns/seal/scroll, two sounds, bible 4.1/4.5/5.3, README legend. Full suite 8350 checks, 0 failed; CI (test + mix) green; squash-merged. Burst is code-drawn (consistent with every other spell); the vfx_workbench burst is left as optional polish.

Pass 496: five Tower signs now name the Delver's Pick instead of its id delvers_pick (Foreman's Gate, Kettleforge Stair, Ore Vault, Rail Gallery); a new test fails on any leaked lowercase_with_underscore token in sign/label prose, and the guardian-hall test's stale before/after Foreman text was updated; merged (#553). Resumed after an app restart; the full suite caught the stale test. No visual change, so no captures. PIXELLAB_API_KEY is now set, so the art loop is unblocked for the next pass.
Sean's goal: art on par with AAA pixel-art games. He added 50 USD of PixelLab credits; the loop now puts art ahead of the rubric rotation and can spend all of it
PixelLab key set on this PC and working; the balance is 193 generations (not ~900), so the art budget now covers about two guardians and resumes on each refill
